title: 3 Bed · 3.0 Bath Single-Story Modern Residence
designer_rationale:
The Central Circulation Spine scheme delivers the most balanced integration of functional zoning, bedroom privacy, circulation efficiency, and natural daylight. Its central foyer and gallery act as a clear spine that intuitively separates public gathering areas from the quiet sleeping wing, ensuring acoustic isolation while maintaining a single, efficient circulation path. The central gallery also serves as a daylight conduit, allowing diffused natural light to penetrate deep into the interior, which is especially valuable in a 3‑bed, 2‑bath modern home. Compared to the strict acoustic partition of the Public‑Private Split and the side‑gallery daylight flow of the Side Gallery scheme, the central spine offers superior flexibility for future reconfiguration and a more cohesive spatial hierarchy. Overall, it achieves the highest overall score (88.8) while maintaining perfect privacy and daylight scores, making it the most architecturally coherent choice.
 Site-first planning with South frontage, 5.0ft front setback, and 3 bedrooms across 1158.0 sq ft.

strengths: Intuitive central spine separates public and private zones
Excellent daylight penetration via central gallery
High space efficiency and furniture fit
weaknesses: Potential bottleneck at central foyer if traffic volume increases
Limited flexibility for adding secondary circulation paths
Central spine may constrain future layout modifications
suggestions: Introduce a secondary side corridor to provide alternate circulation during peak use
Use flexible acoustic panels in the central gallery to adapt to changing privacy needs
Incorporate daylight sensors to optimize artificial lighting when natural light is insufficient
